questions.question: Choose the correct order of the following plateaus and mountain ranges from south to north of India.

options.text: Malwa Plateau, Satpura Range, Vindhya Range, and Deccan Plateau
Malwa Plateau, Vindhya Range, Satpura Range, and Deccan Plateau
Deccan Plateau, Satpura Range, Vindhya Range, and Malwa Plateau
Deccan Plateau, Vindhya Range, Satpura Range, and Malwa Plateau

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Deccan Plateau, Satpura Range, Vindhya Range, and Malwa Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Deccan Plateau is located in southern and central India, covering a vast area with its southernmost point.
 
• It is a large triangular plateau covering most of southern India, bordered by the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and the Satpura Range.
 
• The plateau is rich in black soil, making it suitable for cotton cultivation, and is known for its volcanic origin.
 
• Rivers like Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri originate from the Deccan Plateau, flowing eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Satpura Range
 
 
• Located in central India, it runs parallel to the Vindhya Range, forming a natural boundary between northern and southern India.
 
• The range is rich in natural resources, including coal deposits found in regions like Chhindwara and Betul.
 
• Satpura is home to several protected areas, including Satpura National Park, known for its biodiversity.
 
 
 
• Vindhya Range
 
 
• The Vindhya Range lies north of the Satpura Range and plays a crucial role as a cultural and geographical divide between northern and southern India.
 
• It is primarily composed of sandstone and limestone and houses significant mineral reserves.
 
• The range is historically significant, associated with the development of ancient Indian kingdoms and civilizations.
 
 
 
• Malwa Plateau
 
 
• Situated in western Madhya Pradesh and southeastern Rajasthan, it is part of the larger Deccan Plateau.
 
• The region is known for its fertile black soil, ideal for growing wheat, soybean, and cotton.
 
• Malwa Plateau has a rich historical and cultural heritage, with prominent sites like Mandu and Ujjain.

questions.question: Which of the following pressure belt is known as the horse latitude?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Sub tropical high-pressure**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The subtropical high-pressure belt region is also known as the horse latitude. These latitudes are characterized by calm winds and little precipitation.
 
• These ships often encountered areas of high pressure and calm winds, making them unable to sail and resupply for days or even weeks. The crews often ran out of drinking water. To conserve water for their own survival, the sailors would throw the horses into the sea, hence the name horse latitudes.
 
• A horse latitude is a belt of calm air and sea in both the northern and southern hemispheres between the trade winds and the westerlies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The "doldrums" is a popular nautical term that refers to the belt around the Earth near the equator where sailing ships sometimes get stuck on windless waters. This NASA satellite image shows the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, known to sailors around the world as the doldrums.
 
• ** Polar Highs: **At the North and South Poles, between 700 to 900 North and South, the temperatures are always extremely low. The cold descending air gives rise to high pressures over the Poles. These areas of high pressure are known as the Polar Highs.
 
• **the equatorial low: **Near the equator the sea level pressure is low and the area is known as the equatorial low. Along 30° N and 30° S are found the high-pressure areas known as the subtropical highs. Further pole wards along 60° N and 60° S, the low-pressure belts are termed as the subpolar lows.

Thus, Sub tropical high-pressure belt on the globe is otherwise known as the **Horse Latitude**.

 [IMAGE: https://pubs.usgs.gov/gip/deserts/atmosphere/circulate.gif]

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 - a, 2 - d, 3 - b, 4 - c.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamet**, in the **Garhwal region **of the Himalayas in India, is **7756 m **high
 
• **Kangchenjunga**, a part of the Himalayan range present between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim, is** 8586 m **tall
 
• **Nanda Devi**, located in the Garhwal Himalayas, has a height of **7816 m**
 
• **K2**, also known as Mount Godwin-Austen or Chhogori, part of the Karakoram Range, located in the Ladakh Union Territory of India (a disputed territory between India and Pakistan), stands as the second-highest peak in the world with its height of **8611 m**.

***Therefore, the correct option is 1 - a, 2 - d, 3 - b, 4 - c.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kamet:**

 
 
• Kamet is the mountain peak in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It lies very close to the border with Tibet, making its location geopolitically strategical.
 
• The **first successful ascent** to Kamet was made in **1931 by a team led by British mountaineer Frank Smythe.**
 
• At 7756 meters, it is the third-highest peak in India and **29th highest in the world**.
 
• Kamet is known for its unique,** pyramid-like shape** and is often touted as a challenging peak to conquer due to harsh weather conditions and technical climbing sections.
 
 
 
• **Kangchenjunga:**
 
 
• Kangchenjunga, located on the border between Nepal and the Indian state of Sikkim, is the **third-highest mountain in the world.**
 
• It stands tall with a height of** 8586 meters.**
 
• **The first successful ascent** was made by** Joe Brown and George Band in 1955 **as a part of a British expedition. They stopped a few meters short of the actual summit in deference to the local culture that considers the peak sacred.
 
• Kangchenjunga, meaning** "Five Treasures of Snow,"** refers to its five peaks that are said to represent the five repositories of God - gold, silver, gems, grain, and holy books.
 
• The surrounding area is rich in biodiversity and is recognized as a conservation area.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Devi:**
 
 
• Nanda Devi is located in the** Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.**
 
• In addition to being** India's second-highest peak, **it is also considered one of the most beautiful, with its twin peaks providing a stunning spectacle.
 
• Nanda Devi peaks stand at a height of** 7816 meters.**
 
• It is surrounded by the** Nanda Devi National Park, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1988**, home to several endangered species and a unique high-altitude flora.
 
• The peaks of Nanda Devi are considered sacred in local culture, and multiple legends and folk tales revolve around them.
 
 
 
• **K2:**
 
 
• Known as K2, the peak is also dubbed **Mount Godwin-Austen or Chhogori.**
 
• K2, at **8611 meters**, is the **second-highest mountain peak globally**, surpassed only by Mount Everest.
 
• This mountain is reputed to be the most challenging to climb due to its severe weather and difficult ascent routes.
 
• Unlike Everest, which has been successfully climbed by thousands, K2 has only a few hundred successful ascents to its name due to its extreme difficulty.
 
• One significant feature of K2 is the lack of any easy routes to the top. This towering peak is often considered the 'Mountaineers' Mountain' due to its challenging ascent.

questions.question: Which union territory of India has a sea named after it?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**

The elongated chain of islands located in the Bay of Bengal extending from north to south is called Andaman and Nicobar islands. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**Andaman and Nicobar islands:

__
 
• Andaman and Nicobar Islands situated in the Bay of Bengal, run like a narrow chain in the north-south direction extending between 6° 45′ N to 13° 45′ N.
 
• This archipelago is composed of around 265 big and small islands (203 Andaman islands + 62 Nicobar Islands)
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands extend from 6° 45′ N to 13° 45′ N and from 92° 10′ E to 94° 15′ E for a distance of about 590 km.
 
• The total area of this elongated island is 8,249 sq. km.
 
• The Andaman islands are divided into three main islands i.e. North, Middle, and South.
 
• Duncan's passage separates Little Andaman from South Andaman.
 
• The Great Andaman group of islands in the north is separated by the Ten Degree Channel from the Nicobar group in the south.
 
• The Grand Channel is between the Great Nicobar islands and the Sumatra islands of Indonesia.
 
• The Coco Strait is between the North Andaman islands and the Coco Islands of Myanmar.
 
• Port Blair, the capital of Andaman Nicobar Islands lies in the South Andaman.

 
• Among the Nicobar islands, the Great Nicobar is the largest.
 
• It is the southernmost island and is very close to Sumatra island of Indonesia.
 
• The Car Nicobar is the northernmost.
 
• Most of these islands are made of tertiary sandstone, limestone, and shale resting on basic and ultrabasic volcanoes.
 
• The Barren and Narcodam Islands, north of Port Blair, are volcanic islands

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Puducherry:

 
• There are total 4 Districts in Puducherry.
 
• The city is surrounded by Tamil Nadu state, on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, 105 miles (170 km) south of Chennai (Madras).
 
• The Union Territory of Puducherry has been formed consolidating four erstwhile French establishments viz Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.
 
• Karaikal District is in the state of Tamil Nadu and is next to Puducherry in area and population. 
 
• Mahe is surrounded by the State of Kerala and Yanam by the state of Andra Pradesh.
 
• Yanam is one of the regions in the Union Territory of Puducherry which is 870 km away from it.
 
• The town of Yanam lies on the mouth of the Godavari River where it flows into the Bay of Bengal.

'Daman' is the capital of the Union Territory of Daman and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu are part of the union territory.

questions.question: Which of the following passes cuts through Pir Panjal range and links Manali and Leh by road?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Rohtang Pass.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Rohtang Pass**

__
 
• It is a high mountain pass on the eastern end of the Pir Panjal Range of the Himalayas around 51 km from Manali.
 
• It connects the **Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys of Himachal Pradesh.**
 
• It links** Manali and Leh by road**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**There is confusion between Baralacha Pass and Rohtang Pass, but Rohtang Pass is the official answer given by SSC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Banihal Pass**

 
• Banihal Pass is a mountain pass across the Pir Panjal Range at a maximum elevation of 2,832 m.
 
• It connects the Kashmir Valley in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir to the outer Himalayas and the plains to the south.

**Baralachala Pass**

 
• It is a high mountain pass in the Zanskar range, connecting the Lahaul district in Himachal Pradesh to Leh district in Ladakh.
 
• It is situated along the Leh–Manali Highway.

__

questions.question: The central stretch of the Western Coastal Plains of India is known as the:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The central stretch is called the Kannad Plain
 
• It is primarily located in the state of Karnataka.
 
• It extends from the **Arabian Sea** in the west to the foothills of the **Western Ghats** in the east.
 
• The Kannada Plain is characterized by a mix of flat land and low-lying hills, making it less rugged compared to the adjacent Western Ghats.
 
• The soil in the Kannada Plain is primarily **alluvial** and **lateritic**, conducive to farming

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6db57fadbe13a39345f50aaa968c0b5bd4c67f3c78c787a2625a2bcf7a4159b9.png]

__
 
• The Peninsular plateau is flanked by stretch of narrow coastal strips, running along the Arabian Sea on the west and the Bay of Bengal on the east.
 
• The Western Coastal Plains
 
 
• The western coast, sandwiched between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, is a narrow plain.
 
• It consists of three sections; the northern part of the coast is called the Konkan__ (Mumbai – Goa),
 
 
• while the southern stretch is referred to as the Malabar Coast.
 
 
 
• The rivers flowing through this coastal plain do not form any delta.
 
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains 
 
 
• The eastern coast are the plains along the Bay of Bengal are wide and level.
 
• In the northern part, it is referred to as the Northern Circar, while the southern part is known as the Coromandel Coast.
 
• There are well-developed deltas here, formed by the rivers flowing eastward in to the Bay of Bengal and include the deltas of the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna and the Kaveri.

questions.question: Which sub-division of Himalayas are famous for Karewa formations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kashmir Himalayas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sub-division of Himalayas famous for **Karewa formations** is the **Kashmir Himalayas**.
 
• Karewas are lacustrine deposits (deposits in lake beds) found in the Kashmir Valley.
 
• These formations consist of unconsolidated gravel and mud, which are important for agriculture, particularly for the cultivation of saffron.
 
• The **Kashmir Himalayas** are known for their unique geological formations and play a significant role in the region's agriculture and ecology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayas are divided into various sub-divisions based on geographical and ecological characteristics, including the **Punjab Himalayas, Kumaon Himalayas, Nepal Himalayas, Assam Himalayas, and others**.
 
• The **Kashmir Valley** is located between the Great Himalayas and the Pir Panjal range.
 
• Besides Karewas, the Kashmir Himalayas are also known for their picturesque landscapes, rich biodiversity, and cultural heritage.
 
• The region faces several environmental challenges, including deforestation, soil erosion, and the impacts of climate change.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a regional name for East Coast (or part of it) of India?

__
 
• The Western Ghats:

 
 
• The western ghat is the mountain range parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula.
 
• The total length of the western ghat is around 1600 km.
 
• The western ghat region is spread from Tapti to Kanyakumari.
 
• It passes through the Indian states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Goa, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
 
• Anamudi is the highest peak of the western ghat.
 
• All important rivers of Peninsular India originate from the western ghat.
 
• The major hill stations of the western ghat are Amboli ghat, Matheran, Mahabaleshwar, Panchgani, and Kudremukh.
 
 
 
• Eastern Ghats:
 
 
• A discontinuous range of mountains along India's eastern coast runs parallel to the Bay of Bengal. 
 
• They are eroded and cut through by the four major rivers of peninsular India, Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna and Kaveri. 
 
• Some of the important ranges include the Shevaroy hills, Javadi hills, the Palconda range, the Nallamala hills, the Mahendragiri hills, etc.
